findings.problem: The note filename is “named from the title,” but the spec defines no normalization, collision, length, or path-separator rules. A title containing `/`, `..`, control characters, or a conflicting normalized name could escape the intended topic directory or overwrite another note.
findings.suggestion: Define a safe, deterministic title-to-filename encoding, reject unsafe or empty titles, handle collisions explicitly, and require no-follow-link checks for every component and file operation.

findings.problem: The required update-before-create behavior is not implementable as specified. `save` accepts a title and body, but no existing-note identifier or deterministic matching algorithm is defined; “if the idea belongs to” an existing note is a semantic decision with no testable rule.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit note identifier/target option, or specify a deterministic matching and disambiguation algorithm, including the behavior when multiple notes could match.

findings.problem: The review-to-keep workflow is underspecified and internally incomplete. `review` emits a digest, while the prose says the agent applies free-form owner instructions such as dropping or merging notes, but no command, input format, or digest update rules define how those decisions are applied before `keep`; consequently the acceptance criterion that `keep` moves only the intended drafts cannot be verified.
findings.suggestion: Specify the owner-response protocol and its effect on drafts/notes, make the resulting set and digest explicit, and require `keep` to validate that exact post-review set.

findings.problem: Expiry has no defined trigger or visibility semantics. The spec says drafts are moved after 30 days, but does not say whether this occurs during save, list, review, wings, or a scheduled process; archived drafts are also not defined for listing, counts, or recovery. The 30-day acceptance criterion is therefore not operationally testable.
findings.suggestion: Define which command performs expiry, how age is computed, whether it is atomic and idempotent, and how archived drafts appear in or are excluded from `list` and `wings`.

summary: The spec has unresolved safety and workflow gaps around title-derived paths, note selection, review decisions, and draft expiry.
